result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings (including the shared rules in the module docstring) and fixed all of them. After the fix, all 150 rules match their docstrings across a range of quantities and unit prices.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | Discount started only above 12 units (`qty > 12`), but the docstring says 12 or more | `qty >= 12` |
| 47 | Discount started at 101 units instead of 100 | `qty >= 100` |
| 150 | Discount started only above 50 units (`qty > 50`) | `qty >= 50` |
| 18, 49, 84 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, but the shared rule says round down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 42, 111 | Marked "whole" (discount on every unit), but only units above the threshold were discounted | Changed to `base * pct // 100` |
| 68 | The 50,000 won cap only applied once the discount exceeded 100,000 won, so discounts between 50,000 and 100,000 won weren't capped | Always apply `min(disc, 50000)` |
| 69 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount (which the shared rule forbids) | Calculate 12% of the full amount, then cap the discount at 100,000 won |
| 99 | Docstring says 7%, code used 8% | Changed to 7% |
| 117 | Docstring says 3%, code used 4% | Changed to 3% |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each docstring, builds the expected calculation from it and the shared rules, and compares it with the real function. It covered quantities 0–259, 500, 1,000 and 5,000 against 16 unit prices. Before the fix it flagged exactly these 12 rules; after the fix it found 0 mismatches. The script is in `/tmp/chk/` and isn't part of the repo. I only changed the calculation lines in these 12 functions; nothing else in the file was touched.

STATUS: DONE
